Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-3140", "title": "Seasonal Affective Disorder", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression that comes and goes with the seasons."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It usually starts in the late fall and early winter and goes away during the spring and summer."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Some people do have episodes of depression that start in the spring or summer, but that is a lot less common."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Symptoms of SAD may include: Sadness Gloomy outlook Feeling hopeless, worthless, and irritable Loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy Low energy Difficulty sleeping or oversleeping Carbohydrate cravings and weight gain Thoughts of death or suicide SAD is more common in women, young people, and those who live far from the equator."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "You are also more likely to have SAD if you or your family members have depression."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Researchers have found that people with SAD may have an imbalance of serotonin, a brain chemical that affects your mood."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Their bodies also make too much melatonin, a hormone that regulates sleep, and not enough vitamin D."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The main treatment for SAD is light therapy."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The idea behind light therapy is to replace the sunshine that you miss during the fall and winter months."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "You sit in front of a light therapy box every morning to get daily exposure to bright, artificial light."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "But some people with SAD do not respond to light therapy alone."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Antidepressant medicines and talk therapy can reduce SAD symptoms, either alone or combined with light therapy."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Mental Health"}]}, {"id": "MLP-279", "title": "Heart Valve Diseases", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Heart valve disease happens when one or more of your heart valves don't work well."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your heart has four valves: the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The valves have flaps that open and close."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The flaps make sure that blood flows in the right direction through your heart and to the rest of your body."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "When your heart beats, the flaps open to let blood through."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Between heartbeats they close to stop the blood from flowing backwards."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "If one or more of your heart valves doesn't open or close correctly, it can affect your blood flow and strain your heart."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Fortunately, treatment helps most valve diseases."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What are the types of heart valve diseases?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Heart valves can have three basic kinds of problems: Regurgitation , or backflow, happens when the flaps of a valve don't close tightly."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "This allows the blood to leak backwards."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "A common cause of regurgitation is prolapse, where the flaps of the valve flop or bulge back."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Prolapse most often affects the mitral valve ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Stenosis happens when the flaps of a valve become thick, stiff, or stuck together."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This prevents the heart valve from opening all the way."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Not enough blood can pass through the valve."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Aortic valve stenosis is a common type of stenosis."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It affects the valve that controls blood flow into the large artery that carries blood out of the heart to the body."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Atresia happens when a heart valve did not form properly and does not have an opening for blood to pass through."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Sometimes a valve can have both regurgitation and stenosis."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Some people are born with heart valve disease."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "This is called congenital heart valve disease."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "It can happen alone or along with other congenital heart defects ."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Heart valve disease can also develop over time as you get older or have certain conditions that affect the heart."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Who is more likely to develop heart valve diseases?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Your chance of having heart valve disease is higher if: You are older."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "With age, the heart valves can become thick and stiff."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "You have or have had other conditions that affect your heart and blood vessels."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "An untreated strep throat can become rheumatic fever, which can harm the heart valves."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Today, most people take antibiotics to cure strep throat before it can cause heart valve damage."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "This is a rare infection in the lining of the heart and heart valves."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "It is usually caused by bacteria in the bloodstream."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Coronary artery disease , especially when it affects the aorta (the large artery that carries blood from the heart to the body)."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "A family history of early heart disease: A father or brother who had heart disease younger than 55."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "A mother or sister who had heart disease younger than 65."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "You were born with an aortic valve that wasn't formed right."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Sometimes this will cause problems right away."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Other times, the valve may work well enough for years before causing problems."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "What are the symptoms of heart valve diseases?"}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Many people live their whole lives with a heart valve that doesn't work perfectly and never have any problems."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "But heart valve disease may get worse slowly over time."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "You may develop signs and symptoms, such as: Shortness of breath (feeling like you can't get enough air) Fatigue Swelling in your feet, ankles, abdomen (belly), or the veins in your neck Chest pain when you're physically active Arrhythmia , a problem with the rate or rhythm of your heartbeat Dizziness or fainting If you don't get treatment for heart valve disease, the symptoms and strain on your heart may keep getting worse."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "What other problems can heart valve diseases cause?"}, {"id": "S043", "text": "When the valves don't work well, your heart has to pump harder to get enough blood out to the body."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Without treatment, this extra workload on your heart can lead to: Heart failure Stroke Blood clots Sudden cardiac arrest or death How is heart valve disease diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Your health care provider may listen to your heart with a stethoscope and hear that your heart makes abnormal sounds, such as a click or a heart murmur."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "These sounds may mean a valve isn't working normally."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "The provider will usually refer you to a cardiologist, a doctor who specializes in heart diseases."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "The doctor will also listen to your heart and will do a physical exam."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "You will also likely need to have one or more heart tests ."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "What are the treatments for heart valve diseases?"}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Most heart valve problems can be treated successfully."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "Treatment may include: Medicines to control your symptoms and keep your heart pumping well Heart-healthy lifestyle changes to treat other related heart conditions Surgery to repair or replace a valve It's possible that you may need surgery, even if you don't have symptoms."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "Fixing the valve can help prevent future heart problems."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "There are many ways to do heart valve surgery."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "You and your doctor can decide what's best for you, based on your valve problem and general health."}, {"id": "S056", "text": "Heart valve repair surgery has fewer risks than heart valve replacement."}, {"id": "S057", "text": "So, when repair is possible, it's preferred over valve replacement."}, {"id": "S058", "text": "In some cases, valve replacement is necessary."}, {"id": "S059", "text": "There are 2 types of replacement valves: Biologic valves made from pig, cow, or human tissue."}, {"id": "S060", "text": "These valves tend to wear out after 10 to 15 years, but some may last longer."}, {"id": "S061", "text": "Mechanical (human-made) valves usually don't wear out."}, {"id": "S062", "text": "But with a mechanical valve, you usually have to take blood thinners for the rest of your life to prevent blood clots."}, {"id": "S063", "text": "And your risk of endocarditis (a heart infection) is higher than with a biologic valve."}, {"id": "S064", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-482", "title": "Parasitic Diseases", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Parasites are living things that use other living things - like your body - for food and a place to live."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You can get them from contaminated food or water, a bug bite, or sexual contact."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Some parasitic diseases are easily treated and some are not."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Parasites range in size from tiny, one-celled organisms called protozoa to worms that can be seen with the naked eye."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some parasitic diseases occur in the United States."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Contaminated water supplies can lead to Giardia infections ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Cats can transmit toxoplasmosis , which is dangerous for pregnant women."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Others, like malaria , are common in other parts of the world."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "If you are traveling , it's important to drink only water you know is safe."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "There are no vaccines for parasitic diseases."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Some medicines are available to treat parasitic infections."}]}, {"id": "MLP-111", "title": "Cervical Cancer", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cervical cancer is cancer that starts in the cells of the cervix."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The cervix is part of the female reproductive system."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It is the lower, narrow end of the uterus (womb), which opens into the vagina (birth canal)."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Cervical cancer usually develops slowly."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Before cervical cells become cancer, they start to look abnormal."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These cells are called \"precancers.\" If they aren't destroyed or removed, they may become cancer cells that grow out of control and spread to other parts of your body."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Screening tests for cervical cancer can help find abnormal cells so you can get treatment to prevent cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "These tests can also find cervical cancer early when it's usually easier to treat."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Almost all cervical cancers are caused by a long-lasting infection with a virus called human papillomavirus (HPV) ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The types that cause cancer are called \"high-risk HPV.\" High-risk HPV is very common."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It can be passed from one person to another through close skin-to-skin touching, usually during vaginal, anal, or oral sex."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Most people who are infected have no symptoms and don't know they have it."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "If you're infected with high-risk HPV, usually your immune system will get rid of it within a year or two."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "But if your immune system can't control the infection, it may last for many years."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Over time, HPV can turn normal cervical cells into abnormal cells."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Without treatment, these cells may keep changing until they become cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Who is more likely to develop cervical cancer?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Cervical cancer is most common in people over age 30."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "If you have a high-risk HPV infection in your cervix, you're more likely to develop cervical cancer if you: Have a weakened immune system because you: Have a disease that harms your immune system, such as HIV ."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Take medicine to control your immune system, such as certain medicines to treat cancer or autoimmune diseases Smoke tobacco or breathe secondhand smoke ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Use birth control pills or have given birth to many children."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Were exposed to a medicine called DES (diethylstilbestrol) before you were born."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Between 1940-1971, DES was sometimes prescribed during pregnancy to prevent miscarriages ."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "DES was later linked to health problems, including cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "What are the symptoms of cervical cancer?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Cervical cancer usually doesn't cause symptoms when it first starts to grow."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "But when it does cause symptoms, they may include: Vaginal bleeding that's not normal for you, such as bleeding after sex or between menstrual periods Vaginal discharge (fluid) that's watery and has a strong odor or contains blood Pelvic pain or pain during sex If cervical cancer spreads to other parts of your body, symptoms may include: Unusual vaginal bleeding or discharge Pelvic pain or pain during sex Difficult or painful bowel movements (poops) or bleeding from the rectum when having a bowel movement Difficult or painful urination (peeing) or blood in your urine (pee) Dull backache Swollen legs Abdominal (belly) pain Fatigue How is cervical cancer diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "If you have symptoms or had an abnormal result on a screening test for cervical cancer, your health care provider will do more tests to find out if you have cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "They will: Ask about your medical history and your family health history Do a pelvic exam Suggest tests to diagnose or rule out cervical cancer, including: Colposcopy , a procedure using a device called a colposcope, which helps your provider examine your cervix for abnormal areas Cervical biopsy , a procedure to remove a tissue sample from your cervix so that it can be examined under a microscope to look for signs of cancer."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Most biopsies can be done in your provider's office What are the treatments for cervical cancer?"}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Different treatments are available for cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "The best treatment for you depends on your health, how much cancer you have, whether it has spread, and which treatment you prefer."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "You may have more than one treatment, including: Surgery to remove the cancer."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Radiation therapy , which uses high-energy x-rays or other types of radiation to kill cancer cells or keep them from growing."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "The therapy may use radiation from a machine, or a radioactive substance may be placed in your body near the cancer."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Chemotherapy (chemo), which uses special medicines to shrink or kill the cancer."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "The medicine may be pills, or it may be given through a vein (by IV)."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Sometimes, both types of chemo are used."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Targeted therapy , which uses special medicines to block the growth and spread of cancer cells."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Immunotherapy , which helps your immune system fight cancer cells."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Almost all cervical cancer can be prevented by: HPV vaccination ."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "HPV vaccines provide the most protection if you get them before you're exposed to HPV."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "So, it's best to get vaccinated before you become sexually active."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Medical experts recommend vaccinating children between ages 9 and 12."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Two types of screening tests may be part of your routine health checkup."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Both tests use a sample of cervical cells that your provider collects with a swab: A Pap smear checks for abnormal cells so they can be treated before they become cancer An HPV test checks for high-risk HPV infections that can cause cancer."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Getting the right follow-up treatment if a screening test finds abnormal cells and/or high-risk HPV."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "You can lower your risk for cervical cancer by not smoking."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Using condoms correctly during sex lowers your risk of getting an HPV infection, but doesn't prevent it completely."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Condom use has been linked to fewer cases of cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "If you or your partner is allergic to latex, you can use polyurethane condoms."}]}, {"id": "MLP-5334", "title": "Oxygen Therapy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Oxygen is a gas that your body needs to work properly."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your lungs absorb oxygen from the air you breathe."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The oxygen enters your blood from your lungs and travels to your organs and body tissues."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Certain medical conditions can cause your blood oxygen levels to be too low."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Low blood oxygen may make you feel short of breath , tired, and confused."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Oxygen therapy can help you get more oxygen."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Oxygen therapy is a treatment that provides you with extra oxygen to breathe in."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It is only available through a prescription from your health care provider."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You may get it in the hospital, another medical setting, or at home."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Some people only need it for a short period of time."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Others will need long-term oxygen therapy."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "There are different types of devices that can give you oxygen."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Others use an oxygen concentrator, which pulls oxygen out of the air."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "You will get the oxygen through a nose tube (cannula), a mask, or a tent."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The extra oxygen is breathed in along with normal air."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "There are portable versions of the tanks and oxygen concentrators."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They can make it easier for you to move around while using your therapy."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "You may need oxygen therapy if you have a condition that causes low blood oxygen, such as: COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) Pneumonia COVID-19 A severe asthma attack Late-stage heart failure Cystic fibrosis Sleep apnea What are the risks of using oxygen therapy?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Oxygen therapy is generally safe, but it can cause side effects."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "They include a dry or bloody nose, tiredness, and morning headaches."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Oxygen poses a fire risk, so you should never smoke or use flammable materials when using oxygen."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If you use oxygen tanks, make sure your tank is secured and stays upright."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "If it falls and cracks or the top breaks off, the tank can fly like a missile."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is a different type of oxygen therapy."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "It involves breathing oxygen in a pressurized chamber or tube."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "That allows your lungs to gather up to three times more oxygen than you would get by breathing oxygen at normal air pressure."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "The extra oxygen moves through your blood and to your organs and body tissues."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "HBOT is used to treat certain serious wounds , burns , injuries, and infections."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "It also treats air or gas embolisms (bubbles of air in your bloodstream), decompression sickness suffered by divers, and carbon monoxide poisoning ."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "But some treatment centers claim that HBOT can treat almost anything, including Alzheimer's disease , autism , cancer , and Lyme disease ."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not cleared or approved the use of HBOT for these conditions."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "There are risks to using HBOT, so always check with your provider before you try it."}]}]
